title: Australian Federal Budget 2026 — Key Takeaways (12 May 2026)

bigPicture.theme: Significant tax reform + cost-of-living support + fiscal repair
focusAreas: Economic resilience amid global uncertainty (oil shock/inflation pressures)

measures: $250 annual tax offset for ~13 million workers (from 2027–28)
$1,000 instant tax deduction (no receipts required) continues
Ongoing staged income tax cuts continue from prior reforms
planningLens: Skewed toward earned income; many retirees largely miss out

propertyAndInvestmentTax.headline: Major structural change impacting property/trust strategies
negativeGearing: Limited to new residential properties only from 1 July 2027
capitalGainsTax: Replaced with inflation indexation and minimum 30% tax rate on gains (individuals/trusts)
trustTax: Proposed 30% minimum tax on discretionary trusts (from 2028)
planningLens: Reduces attractiveness of leveraged property investing
Less favourable for high-turnover / realised capital strategies
Trust planning + income splitting materially impacted
Shifts incentives toward new housing supply

measures: Additional support: R&D incentives; start-up and VC measures
planningLens: Positive for SME clients and business owners
Encourages capital investment and reinvestment strategies

agedCare: Additional funding + incentives to expand capacity (e.g., new beds)
ndis: Tightened eligibility → fewer participants; cost savings expected
planningLens: Government attempting to reduce long-term spending pressure
Important for clients relying on aged care / disability support planning

measures: Infrastructure funding to support ~65,000 new homes
Policies aimed at ~75,000 additional homeowners over time
Tax changes designed to reduce investor advantage and improve owner-occupier access
planningLens: Preference for new builds over established property

energyInfrastructureDefence.context: Driven by energy security concerns and geopolitical risks

economicOutlook.trajectory: Deficit improving; long path back to surplus (mid‑2030s)

losers: Property investors (existing strategy less favourable going forward)

keyMessages: Many measures commence from 2027 onwards; existing assets largely grandfathered
actionIdeas: Review trust distribution strategies and long-term viability
Re-assess property strategy: cashflow/new-build focus vs tax-driven negative gearing
Reprice after-tax returns for realised capital gains strategies
Client comms: explain timing/grandfathering to avoid overreaction
